title: Sparse Autoencoders are Topic Models
venue: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026), PMLR 306
subcategory: sparse autoencoders as embedding-space topic models
task: Topic modelling over text and image embeddings
problem: The role of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on embeddings is debated; topic models usually reconstruct bag-of-words and do not transfer across modalities.
architecture: Continuous topic model (an LDA analogue in embedding space) under which the SAE objective with L1 penalty is the MAP estimator. SAE-TM: (1) pretrain an SAE on large text or image embedding corpora to obtain topic atoms; (2) learn a word-emission matrix for the atoms on the downstream data; (3) cluster atom embeddings with k-means and merge atoms into any number of topics without retraining.
llm_or_encoder: GRANITE-R2 text embeddings; ViT-B-16-SigLIP image embeddings; InternVL3.5-14B captions; Phi-4 as LLM judge
key_results: Text, 50 topics (averaged over five datasets): CI 54.31 and CR 77.25 vs best baseline 44.61 and 70.24.
At 500 topics SAE-TM keeps CR 71.22 while TSCTM drops to 17.67.
Diversity is second to TSCTM (e.g. D 3.67 vs 3.87 at 50 topics).
strengths: Formal link between SAEs and topic models; one pretrained SAE serves many datasets and any topic count.
Works across text and images; used to compare image datasets and trace themes in woodblock prints.

limitations.text: SAE feature interpretation and use of activation strengths can still be improved.
Coherence is judged by an LLM (Phi-4) rather than by humans or co-occurrence measures.
